journey.title: Tab out of the visit date into the access notes
journey.goal: Pressing Tab in the open date field moves focus to the next form field so the user can keep typing

functionalJourney.title: Pick a visit date with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day in the calendar fills the visit date field

guards.title: Pick the next day with arrow keys
guards.goal: Arrow keys move the calendar focus and Enter commits the date

plan.root_cause: The datepicker traps focus when open, preventing Tab from moving focus to the next form field (notes). The datepicker's keydown listener does not allow Tab to escape the picker widget.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener to the datepicker element when shown that moves focus to the next focusable element in the DOM when Tab is pressed, and remove the listener when hidden. This ensures Tab exits the datepicker and moves focus to the next logical field (e.g., notes).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while the datepicker is open will move focus to the next focusable element in the form (e.g., the notes field), allowing keyboard users to continue navigating the form without getting trapped in the datepicker widget.
functional_risks: The datepicker may lose its internal Tab navigation functionality (e.g., moving between grid cells) if the custom listener interferes. However, the listener only activates for the Tab key and only when the datepicker is attached to an input field, preserving existing arrow key and Enter interactions.
If no next focusable element exists, Tab will be consumed and focus may appear stuck. This mirrors native browser behavior when Tab is pressed in the last focusable element.
The solution assumes the datepicker is inserted after its associated input field in the DOM, which holds true for the current implementation but may break if the DOM structure changes.
verification_requirements: Tab key pressed in the visit-date input when datepicker is open moves focus to the notes input.
Shift+Tab key pressed in the notes input moves focus back to the visit-date input (should still work via natural tab order).
Arrow keys and Enter still function correctly within the datepicker grid for date selection.
Datepicker opens/closes correctly via mouse and keyboard interactions.
No JavaScript errors are introduced in the console.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's keydown listener (onKeydown) consumes the Tab key and prevents default browser focus navigation, trapping focus in the datepicker widget instead of allowing Tab to move to the next form field (notes).
plan.repair_strategy: Wrap the datepicker's keydown listener to ignore Tab key events, allowing the browser's natural focus order to move focus to the next focusable element (the notes input) when Tab is pressed while the datepicker is open.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab in the open visit date field moves focus to the access notes field, allowing keyboard users to continue filling the form without being trapped in the datepicker.
functional_risks: If the datepicker internally uses Tab for any navigation (unlikely, as it uses arrow keys), that behavior would be lost.
Shift+Tab from the notes field should still move focus back to the visit-date input via natural tab order.
Arrow keys, Enter, Escape, and other datepicker shortcuts remain unaffected.
verification_requirements: Tab key pressed in the visit-date input when datepicker is open moves focus to the notes input.
Shift+Tab key pressed in the notes input moves focus back to the visit-date input.
Arrow keys and Enter still function correctly within the datepicker grid for date selection.
Datepicker opens and closes correctly via mouse and keyboard interactions.
No JavaScript errors are introduced in the console.
